content.text:
I submitted index 5 (Mn 0.23, Sb 0.77) as the best composition. At 3.1e-7 A, it had the highest photocurrent of the three I could measure.

| Index | Mn fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 0.50 | -2e-8 |
| 3 | 0.31 | 1.4e-7 |
| 5 | 0.23 | 3.1e-7 |

- **Trend:** photocurrent went up as the Mn fraction went down. The Mn-rich end (1:1 Mn:Sb) showed essentially no photoactivity.
- **Model predictions:** the stability model puts the Mn:Sb 1:2 compound on the convex hull (energy above hull 0 eV/atom). The band-gap model predicts about 2.19 eV for a Mn 0.2 phase and 1.84 eV for the 1:1 phase, both below the 3.22 eV illumination. It gave 0.016 eV for the 1:2 compound, which I treated as unreliable.
- **What's left open:** the trend was still rising at the last point, so more Sb-rich compositions (Mn below 0.2) could be better. I had no merit measurements left to test them.
- **Unused budget:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in the films weren't checked.
